title: Typing Words
objective: Type common English words and letter combinations accurately, including correctly capitalised proper nouns.
lessonSummary:
Once individual letters feel natural, the next step is typing whole words without breaking rhythm — your fingers should start recognising common letter patterns (like "th", "ing", "tion") as a single motion rather than separate keystrokes. This is also a good moment to build the habit of capitalising proper nouns correctly as you type (names, places, brand names), since fixing capitalisation after the fact wastes time in real work.

Typing words well is about smoothness, not just speed — a steady, even pace with fewer corrections beats a fast burst full of mistakes.
keyFocusAreas: Type common letter combinations in longer words.
Type proper nouns with capitalized letters.

tasks.title: Practice — Typing Words
tasks.instructions: Type a list of 15 common words, including at least 3 proper nouns (names/places), for 5–10 minutes. Record your accuracy and note any words you kept mistyping.
tasks.learningObjective: Build accurate whole-word typing, including proper noun capitalisation.

tasks.learningObjective: Apply accurate word typing to a realistic data-entry scenario.
